name: Montreal
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Montreal: due diligence, asset research and litigation support under Quebec civil law and licensing rules.
hero_lede: Montreal is Quebec's commercial capital and a centre for aerospace, artificial intelligence, life sciences and transatlantic trade. TDSC scopes investigative consulting from Nashville for matters touching the city, working from public records and coordinating Quebec-licensed investigators and the client's Quebec counsel where local work is needed.
intro: Montreal is Canada's second-largest metropolitan area. The 2021 census counted 1,762,949 residents in the city and about 4.29 million in the census metropolitan area. It is the economic centre of Quebec and the country's main French-speaking business market. Investment promotion bodies identify aerospace, artificial intelligence, clean technology, defence and security, and life sciences as leading sectors, alongside engineering, pharmaceuticals, video games, finance and logistics. The Port of Montreal links the St. Lawrence to Atlantic shipping routes, and the city hosts international organisations including the International Civil Aviation Organization. Business is conducted in French and English, and legal work sits within Quebec's civil law tradition rather than the common law used elsewhere in Canada.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Montreal for reasons that reflect this mix. Aerospace, defence and engineering groups based in the city run global supply chains and public contracts that carry procurement and integrity exposure. Technology and life sciences companies attract investment that calls for scrutiny of founders, intellectual property ownership and related parties. Real estate and construction have historically drawn attention for collusion and organised crime links, which keeps background research on contractors and developers relevant. Litigators and creditors also need help locating assets and reconstructing corporate histories under Quebec procedure. The work typically combines Quebec registers and court records in French with research in the other countries where a subject operates.

matters.title: Aerospace and defence supplier diligence
matters.text: Montreal's aerospace and defence cluster relies on international suppliers, agents and offset partners. We research ownership, political exposure, export control history and litigation of counterparties so that compliance teams can assess bribery and sanctions risk before contracts, acquisitions or partner onboarding.

matters.title: Construction and real estate integrity
matters.text: Construction and development in Quebec have faced public inquiry into collusion and infiltration by organised crime. We review contractor and developer ownership, prior enforcement, related companies and court records to help lenders, investors and public bodies identify integrity concerns before awarding work or funding.

matters.title: Technology and life sciences investments
matters.text: Investors in Montreal AI, biotech and pharmaceutical companies need to understand who founded and controls them, whether key intellectual property is properly held and whether management has prior disputes. We combine Quebec and federal registers, court records and international sources to test the investment narrative.

matters.title: Asset research for Quebec judgments
matters.text: Creditors enforcing judgments or arbitral awards in Quebec need to know what a debtor owns there. We research enterprise register filings, land register entries, movable property and court records to identify assets and connected entities, so counsel can decide on seizure or other measures.

matters.title: Transatlantic trade counterparties
matters.text: Montreal's port and French-language networks connect it to Europe and francophone Africa. Importers, exporters and trade financiers need assurance about counterparties operating through Montreal. We trace corporate links across Quebec, France, Belgium and African jurisdictions to identify shell structures and undisclosed interests.

local_context.title: Superior Court in Montreal
local_context.text: The Superior Court of Quebec is the general court of first instance for larger civil and commercial claims, and its Montreal district handles a large share of the province's commercial, insolvency and class action work. Proceedings are governed by the Code of Civil Procedure, and pleadings and judgments are commonly in French. Pre-judgment seizure and other enforcement measures are available under that Code, so asset research is usually planned with Quebec counsel around these procedures.

local_context.title: Quebec investigator licensing
local_context.text: In Quebec, a permit issued by the Bureau de la securite privee is required to work as a private investigator, and investigation agencies also require a licence. This regime is separate from Ontario's, so an investigator licensed in Toronto cannot simply work in Montreal. TDSC does not hold a Quebec licence; surveillance, witness enquiries and other fieldwork in Montreal are carried out by Quebec-licensed professionals coordinated through the client's counsel.

local_context.title: Quebec privacy and personal information agents
local_context.text: Quebec has its own private sector privacy statute, the Act respecting the protection of personal information in the private sector, strengthened by Law 25. Persons who commercially establish files on others and communicate reports on character, reputation or solvency may be personal information agents, which the Commission d'acces a l'information considers likely to include licensed investigation agencies. Agents must register with the Commission. Administrative penalties can reach the higher of 10 million dollars or 2 percent of worldwide turnover.

local_context.title: Enterprise and land registers
local_context.text: The Registraire des entreprises keeps Quebec's public enterprise register and assigns each business a Quebec enterprise number. Information declared by registered businesses is available to the public and is a standard starting point for officers, addresses and filings. Federal corporations are also searchable through Corporations Canada. Real property in Montreal is recorded in the Quebec land register, which identifies registered rights and hypothecs. Attribution of control usually requires combining these with court records.

local_context.title: International organisations and diplomacy
local_context.text: Montreal hosts the headquarters of the International Civil Aviation Organization and other international bodies, and has a substantial consular and non-governmental presence. Matters touching these organisations can raise questions of privileges and immunities and of access to records that differ from ordinary commercial work. Where a matter involves such an institution, TDSC confirms with counsel what may be approached and how before any enquiry begins.

tdsc_approach: TDSC has no office in Montreal and works on Montreal matters from Nashville. We start by confirming with the client's Quebec counsel the purpose of the work, whether litigation in the Superior Court, enforcement, an arbitration, a transaction or an internal review, because Quebec civil procedure and privacy law shape what may be collected and how it is used. Research draws on the Quebec enterprise register, federal corporate records, the Quebec land register, court decisions and French-language media. Fieldwork in Montreal is carried out by professionals holding Quebec permits from the Bureau de la securite privee. Personal information is handled in line with Quebec's private sector privacy statute, and reports are prepared with sources for counsel.

faqs.q: Can a US or Ontario investigator work in Montreal?
faqs.a: Not without Quebec authorisation. A permit from the Bureau de la securite privee is required to work as a private investigator in Quebec, and licences from other provinces do not carry over. TDSC therefore coordinates Quebec-permitted professionals for any surveillance, witness contact or attendance in Montreal, and plans the work with the client's Quebec counsel.

faqs.q: Are Quebec corporate records available in English?
faqs.a: The Quebec enterprise register is public and can be searched online, but many filings, court judgments and land register documents are in French. We review French-language records directly and translate relevant extracts in reports. For federally incorporated companies, Corporations Canada records are available in both official languages, which helps when a subject uses both levels of incorporation.

faqs.q: Does Quebec privacy law affect background investigations?
faqs.a: Yes. Quebec's private sector privacy statute, as amended by Law 25, governs the collection and communication of personal information by enterprises in Quebec. Organisations that commercially compile reports on people may qualify as personal information agents and must register with the Commission d'acces a l'information. We scope collection with counsel so that the purpose and legal basis are documented.

faqs.q: How do you research assets of a Montreal debtor?
faqs.a: We search the Quebec enterprise register for companies and roles, the Quebec land register for immovable property and hypothecs, Superior Court and other court records for prior judgments and seizures, and federal and foreign records where the debtor operates abroad. Findings are sourced so that counsel can assess seizure before or after judgment under Quebec procedure.

faqs.q: Which Montreal sectors most often need integrity due diligence?
faqs.a: Aerospace and defence suppliers, construction and real estate developers, engineering firms with international projects, and technology and life sciences companies raising capital are the most frequent subjects. Each raises different questions, from foreign agents and procurement history to founder backgrounds and intellectual property ownership. We tailor scope to the specific transaction or relationship.
